scenes.heading: Servlets, Style System & Best Practices
scenes.narration: Components. Servlets, Style System & Best Practices. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: Which servlet base class should you use for a read-only GET endpoint?
scenes.heading: SlingSafeMethodsServlet
scenes.body: The speech says servlets are OSGi components that extend SlingSafeMethodsServlet for read-only GET, or SlingAllMethodsServlet for GET and POST.
scenes.narration: Which servlet base class should you use for a read-only GET endpoint? SlingSafeMethodsServlet. The speech says servlets are OSGi components that extend SlingSafeMethodsServlet for read-only GET, or SlingAllMethodsServlet for GET and POST.

scenes.question: How does the speech say to register a servlet by resource type?
scenes.heading: Use @Component(service = Servlet.class) together with @SlingServletResourceTypes specifying resourceTypes, methods, and extensions
scenes.body: The speech provides the exact pattern: @Component(service = Servlet.class) and @SlingServletResourceTypes(resourceTypes = "wknd/components/search", methods = "GET", extensions = "json").

scenes.question: What is the recommended binding approach for Sling servlets in AEM?
scenes.heading: Bind servlets to resource types, not to paths
scenes.body: The speech says the best practice is to bind servlets to resource types and not to paths.

scenes.question: Why are path-bound servlets discouraged according to the speech?
scenes.heading: Because they cannot be access-controlled through the repository and are harder to secure
scenes.body: The speech says path-bound servlets with @SlingServletPaths are discouraged because they cannot be access-controlled through the repository and are harder to secure.

scenes.question: What does the Style System let template authors do?
scenes.heading: Define CSS classes in a policy that content authors can apply to a component without code changes
scenes.body: The speech says the Style System lets template authors define CSS classes in a policy that content authors then apply to a component, without any code change.

scenes.question: Given a scenario where authors need multiple visual variants of the same component, what does the speech recommend instead of creating many near-duplicate components?
scenes.heading: Prefer the Style System and configurable components over copies of nearly identical components
scenes.body: The speech says the Style System is a preferred way to offer visual variants rather than creating additional components, and summarizes that configurable components are preferred over copies of nearly identical ones.

scenes.question: Which best-practice summary matches the speech?
scenes.heading: Put logic in Sling Models and markup in HTL; use proxy components; never modify /libs; prefer specific injectors, Resource adaptables where possible, delegation, compatible dialogs, resource-type servlets, code-based config, and the Style System
scenes.body: The speech closes with a summary of best practices: keep logic in Sling Models and markup in HTL; use proxy components; never modify /libs; use specific injector annotations; use Resource as adaptable when possible; use model interfaces and delegation; keep dialogs structurally compatible; bind servlets to resource types; do not hard-code configuration; and prefer the Style System and configurable components over near-duplicate copies.
